design_principles: Federated identity: the user authenticates to each provider independently via OIDC. The orchestrator never holds master credentials.
Billing stays with the provider: Stripe, Vercel, and Supabase each bill the user directly from their own accounts. The AI vendor never intermediates revenue, payment data, or invoicing.

Delegated spend is capped and revocable: agentic_funding grants the orchestrator time-limited, amount-bounded authority to initiate spend on the user's behalf — it is not a billing proxy. Human approval is required above defined thresholds.

Secrets never transit the orchestrator: the connections model pushes secrets directly between providers via ephemeral_oidc tokens. The agent sees reference names and push status only — never secret values.

Minimal blast radius: restricted_scopes and approval_required gates prevent the agent from taking irreversible actions (dns:transfer, billing:upgrade, database:delete) without explicit human approval.
Compliance boundaries are explicit and non-negotiable: KYC, AML, and PCI-DSS requirements are surfaced to the user and owned by the provider. The agent cannot bypass or proxy them.
Every action is auditable: token issuance, API calls, secret references, and resource IDs are logged in an immutable trace the user owns.

Rollback is defined: partial failure triggers a documented teardown. Resources that cannot be auto-destroyed post-compliance-verification (e.g. Stripe accounts post-KYC) are flagged with manual steps.
non_goals: Consolidating billing under an AI vendor. Each provider invoices the user directly.
Replacing provider dashboards. Ship bootstraps a baseline; ongoing management stays in each provider's UI.
Abstracting away compliance. KYC, AML, and PCI requirements are surfaced and owned by the provider.
Storing or transmitting secret values. This manifest is safe to commit. No secret values appear here or in agent context.
Provisioning environments with existing production data. Ship bootstraps clean environments only.

billing_identity._note: Each provider bills this entity directly. The orchestrator facilitates account linking but never intermediates payment flows or holds funds.

commercial_authority._note: The agent may initiate recurring spend on the user's behalf up to these caps. This is delegated authority with human approval gates — not consolidated billing.

user_must_acknowledge: Stripe will perform identity verification (KYC) directly with you before live payments are enabled. The orchestrator cannot bypass or proxy this step.
Your Stripe secret key is never read by the agent. It is pushed directly to your hosting provider via a scoped ephemeral token.
PCI-DSS SAQ-A compliance is your responsibility once live. Stripe's hosted elements handle card data; your server must not.
Stripe accounts cannot be automatically deleted after KYC. If provisioning fails after this step, you must close the account manually at dashboard.stripe.com.

rollback_behavior.manual_steps_if_not: Visit dashboard.stripe.com → Settings → Account → Close account. This step cannot be automated post-KYC.

connections._note: Secrets are never read by the orchestrator. Each wire instructs the source provider to push the named secret directly to the destination provider's secret store via a scoped ephemeral_oidc token. The agent sees only the reference name and push status.

dependency_graph._note: User must review and confirm all compliance items (KYC, PCI, DNS delegation) before any provisioning begins. This step cannot be skipped.

oidc._note: The issuer is the MCP-compatible agent identity. In production this would be the agent vendor's OIDC discovery endpoint (e.g. Anthropic's for Claude). Providers verify the agent's identity against this issuer before issuing a Delegation Token.

exceptions.reason: Stripe accounts cannot be automatically deleted after KYC/AML verification has been initiated. Manual closure required at dashboard.stripe.com.

mcp_extension.description: Ship is proposed as a formal extension to the Model Context Protocol, owned and maintained by Anthropic. Providers implement Ship as MCP servers exposing the ship/v1 tool namespace. Any MCP-compatible agent can then orchestrate provisioning without provider-specific integration.

protocol.description: Providers implement Ship as an MCP server extension. Compatibility is declared via MCP's existing well-known discovery mechanism and verified against the Ship compliance test suite published alongside the extension spec.

required_endpoints.description: Accepts the agent's OIDC token, presents an OAuth2 PKCE consent screen directly to the user (not proxied through the agent), and returns a scoped Delegation Token.
Provisions the declared resource. Idempotent — a second call with the same session_id and resource spec must not create a duplicate.
Instructs this provider to push a named secret reference to a destination provider's /mcp/secret-receive over mTLS. The agent is not in the data path.
Receives secret values from a source provider and writes them to this provider's secret store. Accepts only inter-provider tokens scoped to this session.
Destroys all resources provisioned under this session_id. Idempotent. Returns a list of destroyed resources and any skipped with reasons.
Streams audit events for this session as newline-delimited JSON. The user — not the agent — controls retention and export.

coordination_model.governance: Ship is proposed as an extension to the Model Context Protocol, owned by Anthropic. The path to adoption: (1) submit extension PR to modelcontextprotocol/specification, (2) Anthropic publishes compliance test suite, (3) Stripe, Vercel, and Supabase implement six MCP server endpoints as reference implementors, (4) any provider that passes the test suite is listed in the MCP registry as Ship-compatible. No new standards body required.

incentives.Vercel: Developers arrive with a configured project rather than an empty dashboard. Reduced activation drop-off.
incentives.Supabase: Agent-driven provisioning reduces time-to-first-query. Higher activation rate.
incentives.Stripe: Faster path from account creation to first test payment. Stripe retains full KYC gate and direct billing relationship.
incentives.Anthropic_and_agent_vendors: A more capable agent is a more valuable agent. Each new provider that joins compounds the /ship capability.
incentives.Founders: Hours of dashboard-hopping replaced by a single guided session. No secret copy-paste risk from day one.
